items.name: Anthropic Claude Fable 5.2
items.summary: Anthropic's most capable model for technical work, launched 9 November. It tops the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at 64.6, generates outputs up to 30% faster than Fable 5.1, and costs 20% less at $8/$40 per million tokens; the same underlying model ships as Mythos 5.2 for vetted cybersecurity and life-science users.

items.name: Meta Muse Ember
items.summary: Meta's smallest and most efficient model, launched 9 November for the high-volume work AI agents repeat all day: tool calls, coding subtasks, routing and extraction. At $0.10/$0.50 per million tokens with a 1M-token context, it matches Claude Haiku 5.5 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at about a third of the cost per task.

items.name: NVIDIA GR00T 2
items.summary: NVIDIA's open world-action model for robots, unveiled 9 November at CoRL. Trained partly on 100,000 hours of first-person human video, it completed 40 of 50 unseen manipulation tasks with no task-specific demonstrations; Isaac Lab 3.0 shipped alongside it.

items.name: Tencent Hy4
items.summary: Tencent's 770B-parameter mixture-of-experts flagship, launched 4 November — the first Hy model with vision input and computer use, with a 1M-token context window. It is available via Tencent Cloud TokenHub and OpenRouter, with open weights promised but not yet released.

items.name: Cognition SWE-2 Flash
items.summary: Cognition's fast coding model, launched 4 November and post-trained from Thinking Machines' Inkling-Small (276B total, 12B active parameters). It runs about 3x faster than SWE-2 at a fifth of the price and is free in Devin Desktop and CLI through 30 November, though its weights are withheld over cyber-misuse risk.
